name: Poqomam, Southern
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Los restantes idiomas Mayances tienen sistemas de acentuación y el acento es completamente predecible en el vocabulario nativo. Existen cuatro tipos básicos de sistemas de acentuación (los clíticos no tienen acento): Tipo A: acentúa la sílaba más pesada de cada palabra, ej. Wasteko, Mam del Norte. Tipo B: acentúa la primera sílaba de la raíz de una palabra en medio de frase; acentúa la última vocal de una palabra en posición final de frase, ej. Tzeltal, Q'anjob'al. Tipo C: acentúa la penúltima sílaba, ej. Mam del Sur, Ixil. Tipo D: acentúa la última vocal de cada palabra, ej. K'iche', Mam Occidental (=Takaneko), Q'eqchi', Poqom.
new_statements.translation: The remaining Mayan languages have stress systems and stress is completely predictable in native vocabulary. There are four basic types of stress system (clitics bear no stress): Type A: stresses the heaviest syllable of each word, e.g. Huastec, Northern Mam. Type B: stresses the first syllable of the root of a word phrase-medially; stresses the last vowel of a word in phrase-final position, e.g. Tzeltal, Q'anjob'al. Type C: stresses the penultimate syllable, e.g. Southern Mam, Ixil. Type D: stresses the last vowel of each word, e.g. K'iche', Western Mam (=Takaneko), Q'eqchi', Poqom.
new_statements.citation: Kaufman, Terrence. 1990. Algunos rasgos estructurales de los idiomas Mayances con referencia especial al K'iche'. In Nora C. England & Stephen R. Elliott (comps.), Lecturas sobre la lingüística maya, pp. 59-114. La Antigua Guatemala: Centro de Investigaciones Regionales de Mesoamérica (CIRMA) / South Woodstock, VT: Plumsock Mesoamerican Studies. ISBN 0-910443-05-X.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final vowel (final syllable) of every word; it is fully predictable in native vocabulary; clitics are unstressed. Poqom (Kaufman's cover term for Poqomam and Poqomchi') is listed as a Type-D (fixed final stress) language.
new_statements.exceptions: Clitics do not bear stress ('los clíticos no tienen acento'); predictability is asserted for native vocabulary only (loans implicitly excepted).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('cada palabra'); statement is a comparative typology made for 'Poqom' as a whole, not specifically for the Palín (Southern) variety. Palín citation forms in Benito Pérez 2016 (IPA with stress marks, all final: [ki.'mikʲ], [tu.'luɬ], [ʔa.'w'aχ], [ri.si.'w'i:ɬ], [kam'.'laχ]) are consistent with it.
new_statements.identity_note: poqo1255 is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for the retired ISO code [pou] 'Poqomam, Southern' = Palín Pocomam (Ethnologue 15: 'Region 20 kilometers south of Guatemala City. Alternate names Palín Pocomam'), merged into Poqomam [poc] (Glottolog poqo1254) by ISO CR 2008-057. The quoted statement (Kaufman 1990) is made at the level of 'Poqom' (Kaufman's cover term for Poqomam + Poqomchi'), not specifically for the Palín variety. Palín-specific corroboration: Benito Pérez 2016 (CIESAS MA thesis,../poqo1253/), whose data are explicitly from Palín ('la de la región sur (Palín)'), marks every polysyllabic IPA citation form with final stress but has no prose statement. The ideal primary source, Santos Nicolás & Benito Pérez 1998 Gramática Poqom, is stated by Benito Pérez 2016 (p. 10) to analyse 'el poqom del municipio de Palín', i.e. exactly this variety.

sources.note: §2.2 Fonología pp. 14-19: no sentence on stress (grep acento/acentu/tónica/sílaba/prosod: no hits); all polysyllabic IPA forms carry a final stress mark: [ki.'mikʲ] kimik, [ʔis.'kʲ'aχ] isk'aj, [ʃa.'ʔaːʍ] xa'aaw, [tu.'luɬ] tulul, [maɬ.'kaʔn] malka'n, [ʔa.'w'aχ] ab'aj, [q'a.'w'is] q'ab'is, [ri.si.'w'i:ɬ] risib'iil, [kʲa.'ʔam'] ka'ab', [kam'.'laχ] kab'laj. pp. 9-10 identify three Poqomam varieties (oriente: S. Luis Jilotepeque etc.; central: Mixco, Chinautla; sur: Palín) and state the 1998 Gramática Poqom analyses Palín.
